messages.subject: Project Cedar — patent schedule and FTO
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Alan,

We're drafting the licence of Larkmoor's LBX-Series technology to Verrell (cosmetics field). Two requests: (1) please confirm the current status of the four families (LBX-P1 to LBX-P4) so we can finalise Schedule 2; and (2) a short freedom-to-operate steer for recombinant collagen / elastin-like / silk-derived actives for cosmetic use in the UK/EU/US, so we can pitch the warranty and third-party-royalty provisions correctly.

No need for a full opinion at this stage — a note we can rely on for the deal would be ideal.

James Osei
Senior Associate
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
This email is confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.snippet: James, Status summary: LBX-P1 granted in GB and via EP (US pending); LBX-P3 granted in GB, EP pendin
messages.subject: RE: Project Cedar — patent schedule and FTO
messages.plaintextBody:
James,

Status summary: LBX-P1 granted in GB and via EP (US pending); LBX-P3 granted in GB, EP pending; LBX-P2 and LBX-P4 pending across the board. I'll send the full register entries for Schedule 2 separately.

On FTO, our searches flagged three third-party rights worth noting: a granted EP on recombinant collagen expression in yeast, a US patent on ELP purification, and a pending EP on cosmetic formulations of recombinant proteins. Our preliminary view is that Larkmoor's current processes don't read onto the two granted rights as properly construed, and the pending application wouldn't be infringed by the contemplated products. I'd keep the third-party-royalty deduction in the licence as a backstop.

Alan Foster
Hartington IP
